review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two theorems whose proofs begin with an identical 7-line block. The block picks an irreducible element of the DVR and proves that the height-one prime's ideal is the span of that element. I grepped the MarkoffModP tree and found the same block in DedekindAuxiliaryCaseI.lean (twice, lines 295–301 and 367–373) and in several other files. A near-identical variant is in RiemannSpaceFinitePlaceIncrement.lean. I found no existing helper lemma for this in the tree. I did not check Mathlib for an existing lemma. The change is modest in size, because the repeated reasoning is short. The case for it is the number of copies across the project. I have not compiled the proposed lemma.

findings.problem: Both theorems start with the same block: choose an irreducible π, then show `vPlace.asIdeal = Ideal.span {π}` by `IsLocalRing.eq_maximalIdeal` followed by `irreducible_iff_uniformizer`. The block appears at lines 52–58 and again at 80–86. Each theorem then calls its source lemma with the same arguments. The same block is also copy-pasted in DedekindAuxiliaryCaseI.lean (lines 295–301 and 367–373), DedekindLeadingTermCancellation.lean, DedekindPerfectResidueCaseI.lean, and elsewhere. The only real content of the 'uniformizer-free' wrappers is this fact, and it is restated each time. Any change to how the uniformizer is chosen would need many edits.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma, ideally in an earlier shared file so that all the copies can use it:

theorem exists_irreducible_asIdeal_eq_span (vPlace : HeightOneSpectrum R) :
    ∃ π : R, Irreducible π ∧ vPlace.asIdeal = Ideal.span {π} := by
  obtain ⟨π, hπ⟩ := IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_irreducible R
  refine ⟨π, hπ, ?_⟩
  calc vPlace.asIdeal = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R :=
        IsLocalRing.eq_maximalIdeal vPlace.isMaximal
    _ = Ideal.span {π} :=
        (IsDiscreteValuationRing.irreducible_iff_uniformizer π).mp hπ

It needs only the existing section variables `[CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R]`. Rewrite case III as
  obtain ⟨π, hπ, hπIdeal⟩ := exists_irreducible_asIdeal_eq_span vPlace
  exact finitePlaceOrderTop_auxiliaryFamily_caseIII_source_lower_bound
    vPlace π hπ hπIdeal D hDIntegral h k epsilon u v hu hv hu1 hv1
and case IV the same way, calling the caseIV source lemma. Hypotheses and imports are unchanged. In DedekindAuxiliaryCaseI.lean the helper can replace the identical blocks, but the later `obtain` uses need `hπ` and `hπIdeal` in the same form.
findings.benefit: The duplicated ideal-equals-span argument is proved once and named. Each wrapper in this file shrinks to two lines. The wrappers then plainly just supply an internally chosen uniformizer. The same lemma can replace the copies in other files, so later changes need one edit instead of many.
